title: Text to Number
statement:
Programs often receive numbers as text, for example from the keyboard or a file. Convert a number written as text into a whole number so you can do math with it.

The input is one line holding a whole number written as text, between -1000000000 and 1000000000. It may start with a minus sign or with leading zeros. Print twice its value as a whole number.

Input:

```text
21
```

Expected output:

```text
42
```
hints: Doubling the text itself does not do math. In some languages it repeats the text instead.
Every language has a built-in way to turn text into a whole number. Convert first, then multiply.

text = input().strip()

python.solution:
def double_text(text: str) -> int:
    number = int(text)
    return number * 2


text = input().strip()
print(double_text(text))
